{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Breakfast|Breakfast]]

A '''tortilla española''' (or Spanish omelette) is a mixture of fried potatoes and onions set in eggs, fried to make a dish somewhat akin to a [[Cookbook:Quiche|quiche]] which may be eaten like a [[Cookbook:Pizza|pizza]].

The following recipe makes a 10-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (25 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) omelette that will feed from one to four persons.

==Ingredients==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* About ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] + 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 6 medium [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]]
* 1 white [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]

==Procedure==

# Heat the garlic and a small amount of oil in a 10-inch [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] until garlic is browned.
# Add the rest of the oil and heat to about 375°F (200°C).
# Cube or slice the potatoes and coarsely chop the onion; add to hot oil and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] until brown.
# [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] the potatoes, onions, and garlic and reserve about 2 tablespoons oil.
# [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] eggs in a separate bowl.
# Add potatoes, onions, and garlic to beaten eggs and allow to sit for about 15 minutes.
# Put reserved tablespoons of oil in original 10-inch frying pan and place over low-medium heat.
# Add egg/potato/onion/garlic mixture to frying pan; fry, lifting up edges of tortilla española to allow uncooked egg to run underneath and cook.
# Serve after cooked as a pizza with your choice of toppings: [[Cookbook:Salsa|salsa]], [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]], shredded [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]], [[Cookbook:Chive|chives]], etc., are all very good choices.
